title: Stevenson-Wydler Short-Form Cooperative Research & Development Agreement – Regents of the University of California - Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory – Division of Facilities Planning & Management
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Stevenson-Wyler Short-Form Cooperative Research & Development Agreement between the Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (EOLBNL), and the District, as the latter prepares to reopen its K-12 classroom, and is considering the adequacy of its current heating, ventilation and air-condition systems (HVAC) in classrooms, for EOLBNL to provide technical assistance to the District in its review of guidance and best practices for reducing aerosol transmission risk and to work with District in selecting indoor air quality (IAQ) monitors as part of longer term strategies to ensure adequate ventilation in K-12 classroom, via the Facilities Planning and Management Division, for the term of January 29, 2021, through March 31, 2021, with the District providing $0 cash and a $1,350.00 in-kind contribution and the Regents though its contract with U.S. Department of Energy (USDOE) contributing $10,000.00, subject to available funding.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Ratifies a no-cost research partnership with Berkeley Lab on classroom air quality and ventilation
summary: The district is partnering with the University of California's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, which will give technical help on reducing the spread of airborne germs and on choosing indoor air quality monitors as schools reopen. The district puts in no cash and $1,350 of in-kind contribution, while the University contributes $10,000 through its U.S. Department of Energy contract. The agreement ran from January 29 to March 31, 2021, which began before the board vote.
vendor_name: Regents of the University of California (Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement - R&D Consultants - Burckhalter Elementary School

group: Measure N Commission - February 2, 2021 Jason Gumataotao, Chairperson
title: Measure N Commission - 2020-2021 Budget Modification - Castlemont High School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of Measure N Commission, of a 2020-2021 budget modification request from Castlemont High School transferring the total amount of $7,795.00 from two different strategic actions; Supplies & Materials (no impact, given the time left in the year and nothing has been spent so far on this action) to Consultant Contracts to hire Oakland Kids First to provide stipends for school year and summer internships, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measure N - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Moves $7,795 at Castlemont High to pay Oakland Kids First for student internship stipends
summary: The Measure N Commission recommends shifting $7,795.00 within Castlemont High School's 2020-21 Measure N budget. The money comes from the supplies and materials line, where nothing has been spent so far, and goes to a consultant contract with Oakland Kids First for stipends for school-year and summer internships.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measure N Commission - February 2, 2021 Jason Gumataotao, Chairperson
title: Measure N Commission - 2020-2021 Budget Modification - Skyline High School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of Measure N Commission, of a 2020-2021 budget modification request from Skyline High School transferring $13,125.00 from four different strategic actions; $5,000 from Transportation Costs, $3,125 from Teacher Substitutes, $4,000 from Transportation Costs, and $1,000 from AC Transit/BART Tickets (little to no impact- travel, field trips, conferences and substitutes not needed) to Teacher Salaries Stipends for Extended Contracts for Collaboration / PD Time, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measure N - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Moves $13,125 at Skyline High from travel and substitute funds to teacher collaboration stipends
summary: The Measure N Commission recommends shifting $13,125.00 within Skyline High School's 2020-21 Measure N budget. The money comes from four lines (transportation costs, teacher substitutes and AC Transit/BART tickets) and goes to stipends for teachers on extended contracts for collaboration and professional development time. The request says travel, field trips, conferences and substitutes are not needed, so there is little to no impact.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

summary: This is the third amendment to the district's professional services agreement with The Integral Group, Inc. for the new Fremont High School building project. It adds commissioning services (checking that building systems work as designed) at no additional cost and extends the end date from December 31, 2020 to December 31, 2021, which is 365 more days.

title: Change Order No. 3, Lease Leaseback Agreement – Overaa/Tulum – Foster The Center Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 3, Lease-Leaseback Agreement (LLA) for the Foster The Center Project with Overaa/Tulum (“Contractor”), Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide the construction services delineated in said Charge Order for the Center New Central Kitchen, in the amount of $2,465,319.59, increasing the LLA not to exceed amount from $47,187,998.25 to $49,653,317.84, extending the current completion deadline of February 20, 2018 to February 17, 2021, an additional 361 calendar days. Approval of Change Order No. 3, LLA between the District and Overaa/Tulum/Eclipse is conditioned upon the concurrent approval of Change Orders No. 1 (21-0481) and 2 (21-0482). All other terms and conditions of the LLA remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $2.47M to Overaa/Tulum's construction contract for the Foster The Center central kitchen
summary: This is the third change order to the district's lease-leaseback construction agreement with Overaa/Tulum for the new central kitchen at the Foster The Center project. It adds $2,465,319.59, raising the contract's not-to-exceed amount from $47,187,998.25 to $49,653,317.84, and extends the completion deadline to February 17, 2021. Approval depends on Change Orders No. 1 and 2 also being approved.
source_issue: The text extends the completion deadline from February 20, 2018 to February 17, 2021 but calls this an additional 361 calendar days, which does not match the span between those dates.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (7–0), instead of with the rest of the consent report.
outcome_action: Adopted

summary: This is the first change order to the district's lease-leaseback construction agreement with Overaa/Tulum for the new central kitchen at the Foster The Center project. title: Change Order No. 2, Lease Leaseback Agreement – Overaa/Tulum – Foster The Center Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 2, Lease-Leaseback Agreement (LLA) Between the District and Overaa/Tulum/Eclipse, Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide construction services which includes Various PCOs for additional equipment and fencing as requested by Nutritional Service and extended site security due to schedule extension, scope to address conflicts in the CDs for the New Central Kitchen for the Foster The Center Project, in the amount of $1,358,091.90, increasing the Contract not to exceed amount from $45,829,906.35 to $47,187,998.25, extending the current completion deadline of January 31, 2020 to February 22, 2020 (an additional 22 calendar days), as selected Contractor, pursuant the Change Order. Approval of Change Order No. 2, LLA between the District and Overaa/Tulum/Eclipse is conditioned upon the concurrent approval of Change Order No. 1 (21-0481). presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $1.36M to Overaa/Tulum's Foster The Center kitchen contract for equipment, fencing and security
summary: This is the second change order to the district's lease-leaseback construction agreement with Overaa/Tulum for the new central kitchen at the Foster The Center project. It adds $1,358,091.90 for preliminary change orders covering extra equipment and fencing requested by Nutritional Services, extended site security, and fixes for conflicts in the construction drawings. It raises the not-to-exceed amount from $45,829,906.35 to $47,187,998.25 and extends the deadline 22 days, to February 22, 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
